paragraphs: R. Yoshiyah and R. Yonatan: “For it was stated: R. Yoshiyah and R. Yonatan, etc.” Although tannaim, the formulation is that of an amoraic statement. Apparently they were later tannaim, like R. Chiyya and R. Shimon son of Rabbi: Tosafot Yeshanim, Yoma 57b. This requires investigation, since he appears to have lived in R. Yehudah ben Beteira's time. Menachot 57b: R. Yonatan and R. Yoshiyah, R. Yishmael's students. Yoma 57b, near the end: he disagrees with R. Yonatan. Shabbat 108a has “R. Yoshiyah's words; R. Natan says”; apparently it should read R. Yonatan. Sotah, chapter 4, 24a, near the end: it was taught, etc., R. Yoshiyah's words; R. Yonatan says, etc. People act like three elders: like R. Yoshiyah concerning mixed species; see R. Yehudah ben Beteira and R. Ilai. Pesachim 54a: he disagrees in his father's name with R. Yehudah and R. Nechemyah. R. Yoshiyah said, “I spoke before R. Yehudah ben Beteira”: Sifrei Bamidbar, beginning of Chukat. Sifrei Devarim, Ki Tetze: R. Yoshiyah said, “Three things Zeira told me in the name of the people of Jerusalem, etc.; I presented the words before R. Yehudah ben Beteira.” See there. Shocher Tov, section 36, has R. Yoshiyah the Great; perhaps he is the aforementioned tanna.
